Part A. Decisions

Q1. ASE guideline: are the aortic arch and isthmus required or optional sites for pulsed-wave Doppler in a fetal echocardiogram? The text (p. 689) and Table 6 (p. 693) appear to differ.

☐ Teach as optional (as in Table 6)

☐ Teach as required (as in the text)

☐ State both and explain

If no answer: Wait for the ChatGPT cross-check of claim AS23-014 against the PDF; if the difference is real, teach as optional and note the text.

Affects: Unit F1

Q2. After a normal early (11 to 14 week) heart check, may the course say plainly that the full second-trimester cardiac screen is still required?

☐ Yes, say it plainly as the editor's teaching

☐ Only once a source is added

If no answer: Left out of unit D9 until a source is added.

Affects: Unit D9

Q3. Does the consent held for archive cases cover publication for teaching in a paid product (not only clinical care)?

☐ Yes, wording covers it

☐ No or unsure: re-consent or do not use

☐ Ask the legal advisor

If no answer: No archive clip is published until this is confirmed in writing.

Affects: All clip drills and the case atlas

AS23-005Every fetal study follows the 'as low as reasonably achievable' principle, which governs the choice of modality and the length of the examination; the operator should know the thermal and mechanical indices and limit output and exposure to what is needed.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.B Safety, p. 684not yetF1

AS23-008Both still images and moving clips are required, together with a structured report; the clips cover the axial sweep, the four-chamber view, both outflow tracts, the three-vessel views and the sagittal views of the aortic and ductal arches.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.A Storage, p. 684; III.E, p. 684-688not yetD13, F1

IS23-082Common fetal indications for fetal echocardiography: suspected structural anomaly; extracardiac anomaly associated with heart disease; suspected abnormal function or cardiomegaly; hydrops; persistent tachycardia (180 bpm or more); suspected heart block or persistent bradycardia (110 bpm or less); frequent or persistently irregular rhythm; nuchal translucency 3.5 mm or more; confirmed or suspected genetic abnormality; monochorionic twinning (if resources allow).ISUOG-2023-SCREEN: Table 2, 'Fetal factors', p. 797not yetD8, D11
IS23-083Common patient or familial indications: first-degree relative of the fetus with congenital heart disease; first- or second-degree relative with Mendelian disease and childhood cardiac manifestations; pregestational diabetes regardless of HbA1c; anti-Ro/SSA antibodies; phenylketonuria (unknown status or periconceptional phenylalanine above 10 mg/dL); retinoid exposure; confirmed fetal infection (TORCH or parvovirus B19).ISUOG-2023-SCREEN: Table 2, 'Patient or familial disease or environmental exposure', p. 797not yetD11
IS23-084Fetal echocardiography may be considered for: second-degree relative with congenital heart disease; gestational diabetes diagnosed in the first or early second trimester; nuchal translucency 3.0-3.4 mm; selected teratogens (for example paroxetine, carbamazepine, lithium, sodium valproate); conception by IVF including ICSI; use of ACE inhibitors.ISUOG-2023-SCREEN: Table 2, 'Other indications when fetal echo may be considered', p. 797not yetD9, D11
